Model cards automatically generate a per-prediction explanation for every inference call
Model cards and individual-prediction explanations are functionally identical, so no gap exists

explanation:
Why this is correct:
A model card documents overall characteristics and limitations. Per-prediction explanations (such as SHAP) explain individual decisions. Both are useful.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Billing: no.
• Auto per-prediction explanations: no.
• Identical: no.

Key takeaway: model-level vs. prediction-level transparency.

stem: A team wants to understand which input features most heavily influenced a specific model's prediction for an individual customer record, in order to explain the decision to that customer. Which AWS capability is best suited for this?
explanation:
Why this is correct:
SageMaker Clarify feature attribution (SHAP) shows which features most influenced a prediction.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Cost Explorer: costs.
• Trusted Advisor: best practices.
• Logs Insights: logs.

Key takeaway: why a prediction → Clarify feature attribution.

stem: A company labels chatbot replies 'Generated by AI' and explains which data sources are used. Which principle does this serve?

choices.text: Faster response time for labeled replies
Transparency to users about AI content

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Disclosing that content is AI-generated and its sources helps users calibrate trust, which is part of transparency.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Robustness, cost, speed: unrelated to disclosure.

Key takeaway: tell users when they're dealing with AI.

stem: A financial services company is deciding between a highly interpretable rules-based scoring model and a more accurate but opaque deep learning model for credit decisions, in an industry with strict explainability regulations. Which statement best reflects the tradeoff involved?

choices.text: There is no tradeoff because deep learning models are always both more accurate and more interpretable
Regulatory explainability requirements only apply to rules-based models, not deep learning models
Interpretability and accuracy are unrelated to model choice in regulated industries
Accept slightly lower accuracy or add explainability tooling for the DNN

explanation:
Why this is correct:
The company may accept somewhat lower accuracy from an interpretable model to meet explainability requirements.

Why the other options are wrong:
• No tradeoff: there is one.
• Rules only for rules-based: no.
• Unrelated: they're related.

Key takeaway: interpretability vs. accuracy tradeoff.

stem: A company published a SageMaker Model Card for its resume-screening model but omitted the 'intended uses and limitations' section. As a result, another team began using the model for an unrelated purpose it was never validated for, leading to poor outcomes. Which improvement to the model card would most directly have prevented this issue?

choices.text: Adding more decimal places to the reported accuracy metric
Increasing the font size of the document
Translating the model card into additional languages

explanation:
Why this is correct:
The card should clearly document intended use cases and explicitly out-of-scope uses.

Why the other options are wrong:
• More decimals, larger font, translations: don't address the gap.

Key takeaway: state intended and out-of-scope uses.

stem: A bank's chatbot must refuse investment advice, block hate speech, mask account numbers in responses, and check answers against source documents. Which Bedrock capability covers all of these?
explanation:
Why this is correct:
Guardrails provide denied topics, content filters, sensitive information filters (masking), and contextual grounding checks, applied consistently to prompts and responses.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Agents: task orchestration.
• Fine-tuning: changes model behavior but doesn't enforce policies.
• CloudWatch: monitoring.

Key takeaway: policy controls for GenAI apps → Guardrails.

stem: A company trains a custom model on SageMaker AI. Which task is the company's responsibility under shared responsibility?

choices.text: Physical security of AWS data centers

explanation:
Why this is correct:
AWS secures infrastructure. The customer controls access (IAM), protects data (encryption and classification), and configures the service securely.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Data centers, hypervisors, network hardware: AWS responsibilities.

Key takeaway: customers secure what they put in and who can access it.

stem: Before using a large collection of customer support transcripts stored in Amazon S3 to fine-tune a foundation model, a data science team wants to automatically discover and flag any sensitive information such as credit card numbers or Social Security numbers contained in the files. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this task?
explanation:
Why this is correct:
Macie scans S3 data for PII before it's used to fine-tune a model.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Config: configuration.
• Trusted Advisor: best practices.
• Inspector: vulnerabilities.

Key takeaway: find PII in S3 → Macie.

stem: A financial services company wants its applications running in a VPC to invoke Amazon Bedrock APIs without any traffic traversing the public internet, in order to meet an internal network isolation requirement. Which approach best satisfies this requirement?

choices.text: Create an AWS PrivateLink (VPC interface) endpoint for Amazon Bedrock
Attach an internet gateway and restrict outbound traffic using security groups
Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the Bedrock endpoint
Use a NAT gateway to route Bedrock traffic through a private subnet

explanation:
Why this is correct:
An AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint for Bedrock keeps traffic from the VPC off the public internet.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Internet gateway: internet path.
• CloudFront: not for this.
• NAT gateway: internet path.

Key takeaway: private Bedrock access → interface endpoint.

stem: A company building a RAG-based application needs to track which source documents and versions were used to build and update its embeddings, so it can trace a given model output back to its original data sources for compliance reviews. Which AWS capability most directly supports this data lineage and cataloging need?

choices.text: AWS Glue Data Catalog with metadata tracking

explanation:
Why this is correct:
The Glue Data Catalog with metadata tracking records which source documents and versions feed the RAG application.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Logs Insights: logs.
• Guardrails: filters.
• KMS: encryption.

Key takeaway: data lineage → catalog metadata.

stem: A company is building an autonomous agent using Amazon Bedrock that needs to call internal APIs to look up customer order status but must not be able to modify or cancel orders. Which security practice should be applied when granting the agent's execution role permissions?

choices.text: Grant full access to all APIs in the order management service and rely on the agent's prompt instructions to avoid modifying orders
Share a single IAM user's credentials across all agents in the organization
Apply the principle of least privilege by granting only the specific read-only API actions the agent needs
Grant the role AdministratorAccess so it never encounters permission errors during development

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Grant the agent's role only the specific APIs and actions it needs (least privilege).

Why the other options are wrong:
• Full access: excessive.
• Shared IAM user: insecure.
• AdministratorAccess: excessive.

Key takeaway: agents → least privilege.

stem: A security team suspects that an internal user made an unauthorized change to a company's Amazon Bedrock Guardrail configuration, weakening its content filters. Which AWS service should the team consult first to determine who made the API call and when?
explanation:
Why this is correct:
CloudTrail records who made API changes to AWS resources and when.

Why the other options are wrong:
• CloudWatch metrics: no identity.
• Trusted Advisor: best practices.
• Macie: sensitive data.

Key takeaway: who changed what → CloudTrail.

stem: A customer's security review asks for AWS's ISO 27001 and SOC 2 reports. Where should the company get them?
explanation:
Why this is correct:
Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS's compliance reports and agreements.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Trusted Advisor: best-practice checks.
• Config: resource compliance in your account.
• Inspector: vulnerabilities.

Key takeaway: AWS's own compliance reports → Artifact.

stem: A company wants to continuously verify that every Amazon S3 bucket used for storing AI training data remains encrypted and never becomes publicly accessible, and to automatically flag any bucket that drifts out of compliance. Which AWS service should they use to implement this ongoing configuration compliance check?
explanation:
Why this is correct:
AWS Config with managed rules continuously checks bucket settings, such as encryption and public access.

Why the other options are wrong:
• GuardDuty: threats.
• CloudTrail: API logs.
• Inspector: vulnerabilities.

Key takeaway: continuous configuration compliance → Config.

stem: An organization running generative AI workloads on Amazon EC2 wants to identify known software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure in the instances hosting its model inference endpoints. It separately wants to ensure the endpoints' security group configurations never drift from an approved baseline. Which pairing of AWS services correctly matches each need?

choices.text: AWS Trusted Advisor for both needs
Inspector for vulnerabilities; Config for drift
AWS Config for vulnerability scanning; Amazon Inspector for configuration drift detection
Amazon Macie for vulnerability scanning; AWS Artifact for configuration drift detection

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Amazon Inspector scans EC2 for known software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Trusted Advisor for both: limited.
• Config for vulnerabilities: no.
• Macie and Artifact: data and reports.

Key takeaway: vulnerability scanning → Inspector.

stem: A team wants ongoing recommendations on cost savings, security settings, fault tolerance, and service limits across its account. Which service fits?
explanation:
Why this is correct:
Trusted Advisor checks accounts against best practices in cost, security, fault tolerance, performance, and service limits, with recommendations.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Artifact: compliance reports.
• Macie: sensitive data.
• Audit Manager: audit evidence.

Key takeaway: best-practice recommendations → Trusted Advisor.

stem: A healthcare company must ensure that patient data used to fine-tune its generative AI model, as well as any model artifacts derived from it, never leaves a specific geographic region due to regulatory requirements. Which combination of actions best addresses this data residency requirement?

choices.text: Keep resources in approved Regions, enforced with SCPs
Use a single global Amazon S3 bucket and rely on client-side encryption alone
Enable Amazon CloudFront to cache the model outputs globally for faster access
Rely on the default AWS shared responsibility model without additional configuration

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Restricting training, storage, and inference resources to approved Regions keeps patient data within required boundaries.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Global bucket: violates residency.
• CloudFront global caching: spreads data.
• Default shared responsibility only: not enough.

Key takeaway: data residency → restrict Regions.

stem: A company's internal governance policy requires that logs of all generative AI model inference requests be retained for exactly 400 days and then automatically deleted. Which AWS approach most efficiently enforces this requirement for logs stored in Amazon S3?

choices.text: Manually review and delete objects from the S3 bucket every year
An S3 Lifecycle rule expiring objects at 400 days
Set the S3 bucket to use Reduced Redundancy Storage
Enable S3 Versioning only, without any lifecycle configuration

explanation:
Why this is correct:
An S3 Lifecycle policy expires inference logs automatically after the retention period.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Manual deletion: error-prone.
• Reduced Redundancy: storage class.
• Versioning only: keeps more data.

Key takeaway: automatic retention → lifecycle expiration.

stem: A governance team is evaluating several generative AI use cases, ranging from consuming a public third-party chatbot to fully training a proprietary foundation model in-house, and wants a structured framework to understand how security and compliance responsibilities shift across these scenarios. Which AWS-published framework is designed for this purpose?

choices.text: The AWS Well-Architected Framework Cost Optimization Pillar
The AWS Shared Responsibility Model diagram alone
The Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix
The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) Business Perspective

explanation:
Why this is correct:
The Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix classifies use cases from consuming public apps to building your own models, guiding security controls for each.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Cost pillar: cost.
• Shared responsibility alone: not scoped to GenAI types.
• CAF Business: business adoption.

Key takeaway: scope GenAI security by use case type.

stem: A company's AI governance board currently reviews all deployed generative AI models for bias, safety, and compliance once every two years. After a recent incident where a model's outputs drifted into non-compliant territory months before the scheduled review, leadership asks for a recommendation. Which change best balances governance rigor with operational overhead?

choices.text: Outsource all governance responsibility to the foundation model provider
Eliminate scheduled reviews entirely and rely only on customer complaints to trigger investigation
More frequent, risk-based reviews with monitoring
Keep the two-year cadence but increase the length of each review meeting

explanation:
Why this is correct:
A two-year cadence is too slow for changing models. Move to more frequent, risk-based reviews with continuous monitoring.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Outsource governance: you stay accountable.
• Only complaints: reactive.
• Longer reviews every 2 years: still too infrequent.

Key takeaway: governance cadence should match risk.

stem: An AI governance team needs two distinct capabilities: first, a historical, immutable record of every API call made against their Amazon Bedrock resources for forensic investigation; second, a continuous assessment of whether their S3 data buckets currently comply with an encryption policy. Which statement correctly matches AWS services to these two governance needs?

choices.text: AWS CloudTrail provides the historical API call record; AWS Config provides continuous configuration compliance assessment
A single AWS Config rule can fully replace the need for CloudTrail in both cases
AWS Trusted Advisor is required for both needs since it consolidates CloudTrail and Config functionality
AWS Config provides the historical API call record; AWS CloudTrail provides continuous configuration compliance assessment

explanation:
Why this is correct:
CloudTrail provides the historical record of API calls. AWS Config tracks resource configuration and evaluates compliance.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Config replaces CloudTrail: no.
• Trusted Advisor for both: no.
• Swapped: incorrect.

Key takeaway: activity → CloudTrail; configuration → Config.

stem: An executive says: 'We need AI, not machine learning, and we don't need generative AI because we already have AI.' Which statement corrects this?

choices.text: AI, ML, and GenAI are three unrelated technologies
ML is a rules-only approach that excludes learning from data
GenAI is broader than AI, and ML is a type of GenAI
ML is part of AI; GenAI is part of ML (deep learning)

explanation:
Why this is correct:
AI is the broad field. Machine learning is a subset that learns from data, and generative AI is a subset of ML (deep learning) that creates new content. Having some AI doesn't mean having GenAI capabilities.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Unrelated: they are nested.
• GenAI broader: reversed.
• Rules-only: ML learns from data.

Key takeaway: AI ⊃ ML ⊃ deep learning ⊃ GenAI.

stem: A company lists its data: an order database, support call recordings, JSON clickstream events, and scanned contracts. Which classification is correct?

choices.text: Orders: unstructured; recordings: structured; JSON: unstructured
JSON: structured; orders and recordings: semi-structured
Orders structured; JSON semi-structured; audio/scans unstructured
All four are structured because they are stored digitally

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Structured data fits fixed rows and columns (the order database). Semi-structured data has tags or keys but a flexible schema (JSON). Unstructured data has no predefined model (audio, images, scanned documents).

Why the other options are wrong:
• All structured: storage doesn't define structure.
• Swapped categories: incorrect.

Key takeaway: structure determines the tools you need.

stem: A company compares three purchases: paying per API call to a managed AI service, paying hourly for an endpoint instance, and paying per user per month for an AI assistant. Which pricing models are these, in order?
explanation:
Why this is correct:
Pay-per-request is consumption-based, pay-per-hour for provisioned capacity is instance-based, and per-user subscriptions are seat-based.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Other orders: mismatch the definitions.
• All consumption: ignores the hourly and per-user structures.

Key takeaway: match the pricing model to the usage pattern.

stem: A fraud-detection model's accuracy has declined significantly since deployment, and investigation shows that the distribution of transaction features in production now differs substantially from the training data distribution. This is an example of which reliability risk?

choices.text: Data drift, a primary driver of model drift

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Changes in input data since deployment (data drift) are a primary driver of model accuracy decline.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Explainability failure: no.
• Fairness violation: not indicated.
• Privacy breach: no.

Key takeaway: declining accuracy → check data drift.
